newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil steady, strong crude helps low sulphur.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil steady, strong crude helps low sulphur.

text.p: European fuel oil prices were notionally steady on Monday with higher crude helping low sulphur to hold its newly firmer levels, traders said.
European public holidays meant business was very thin, with the ARA barge market almost completely dormant. Prompt high sulphur fuel oil was unchanged at around $83/$85 fob a tonne.
Paper was firmer into June, with first half physical seen at $85/$86 a tonne.
Low sulphur prices leapt $5 on Friday on a cargo deal at $95 fob, before crude began its spectacular late bull run, which entrenched higher prices.
Perceived U.S. demand for one percent cracked was the cause of the surge, traders said.
"Demand is driven by the States, it's nothing to do with Enel at the moment," said one trader. "The market is on an upturn. It's a trend and whether the demand is really there or not doesn't matter."
U.S. East Coast utility demand was seen falling this week, with natural gas now more attractively priced than one percent fuel, U.S. reports said.
Straight-run fuel levels got a strong boost from crude's strength.
